en: Earth's atmosphere is composed of approximately 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen by volume.
Water expands by about 9 percent in volume when it freezes into solid ice.
Seawater contains roughly 35 grams of dissolved salts per liter of water on average.
Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metals at 3,422 degrees Celsius.
Light travels about 880,000 times faster than sound through air at sea level.
Osmium is the densest naturally occurring element, weighing about 22.59 grams per cubic centimeter.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level but at lower temperatures on Mount Everest.
Milk is a colloidal mixture containing about 87 percent water and 3.5 percent milk fat.
A fire requires at least 16 percent oxygen in the air to continue burning.
Over 99 percent of the visible matter in the universe exists as hot plasma.
Diamond conducts heat about five times better than copper, making it an exceptional thermal conductor.
Solid carbon dioxide, or dry ice, sublimates directly into gas at -78.5 degrees Celsius.
